```
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * index.php — Slim 4 front controller for ScrumMasterTool.
 *
 * Loads environment variables then delegates to the shared app factory
 * (bootstrap/app.php) and calls $app->run().
 */

require dirname(__DIR__) . '/vendor/autoload.php';

// Load .env
$envPath = dirname(__DIR__);
if (file_exists($envPath . '/.env')) {
    $dotenv = Dotenv\Dotenv::createImmutable($envPath);
    $dotenv->load();
}

// Serve compiled Vue SPA for all non-API routes so that client-side
// navigation (Vue Router history mode) works when the page is refreshed.
// Skip if the requested path is an actual file (assets, favicon, etc.)
$uri = $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] ?? '/';
$path = parse_url($uri, PHP_URL_PATH);
$requestedFile = __DIR__ . $path;

if (!str_starts_with($path, '/api/') && !is_file($requestedFile)) {
    $distIndex = __DIR__ . '/dist/index.html';
    if (is_file($distIndex)) {
        header('Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8');
        readfile($distIndex);
        exit;
    }
}

/** @var \Slim\App $app */
$app = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/bootstrap/app.php';

$app->run();
```

Perfect! I've fixed the base path in the Vite configuration. Now the Vue build will generate asset paths like `/dist/assets/...` which matches where the files actually exist on the server.

**To apply the fix:**

1. **Rebuild the frontend locally (or let GitHub Actions do it):**
   ```bash
   cd OrgDocument/Solutions/ScrumMasterTool/frontend
   npm run build
   ```

2. **Commit and push:**
   ```bash
   git add frontend/vite.config.js
   git add public/dist/  # include the rebuilt files if you built locally
   git commit -m "Fix asset paths: set Vite base to /dist/"
   git push
   ```

The GitHub Actions workflow will automatically rebuild the frontend with the correct paths and deploy it. After deployment completes, the website should load correctly with all JavaScript modules.

**What was wrong:**
- Vite was building with  but outputting to `public/dist/`
- This caused HTML to reference `/assets/index-xxx.js`
- But files were actually at `/dist/assets/index-xxx.js`
- The server returned HTML (404 fallback) instead of JavaScript, causing the MIME type error

**The fix:**
- Changed  to `/dist/` so generated paths match the actual file locations
